title: Etale cohomology of one geometric point
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $C=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\bar c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to C$ be a geometric point of $C$ [def-weil-geometric-point] ($\Omega$ any algebraically closed field with a homomorphism $k\to\Omega$, for instance $\bar c=\mathrm{id}_C$). For an abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $C_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] with geometric stalk $F_{\bar c}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], the etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] satisfies $H^q(C,F)=0$ for every $q>0$, and the canonical map $H^0(C,F)\to F_{\bar c}$, the inverse of the isomorphism $F(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(C,F)$ induced by a resolution followed by the germ map $t\mapsto t_{\bar c}$ at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(C,\bar c)$, is an isomorphism of abelian groups, natural in $F$.

proof.text: *$k$ is its own separable closure and the Galois group is trivial.* Let $L/k$ be a finite separable extension and $\alpha\in L$. Its minimal polynomial over $k$ is irreducible and, $k$ being algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], has a root in $k$, hence has degree $1$; so $\alpha\in k$ and $L=k$. Thus $k$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] and $k^{\rm sep}=k$ is a separable closure of $k$, with $G=\operatorname{Gal}(k^{\rm sep}/k)=\{1\}$. The geometric point $\bar c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to C$ [def-weil-geometric-point] is a field homomorphism $k\to\Omega$, i.e. an embedding of $k^{\rm sep}=k$ in the algebraically closed field $\Omega$, and $\bar c$ is the geometric point attached to this embedding in the sense of [lem-exc-field-sections-stalk-invariants].

source.place: Section 03QQ (section-cohomology-point), notation of Theorem 03QT (theorem-equivalence-sheaves-point): $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{sep}/K)$, specialized to $K=k$ algebraically closed

proof.text: *Global sections are the geometric stalk (Lemma 04JM with $G$ trivial).* Apply [lem-exc-field-sections-stalk-invariants] with $K=k$, $K^{\rm sep}=k$, the embedding $k\to\Omega$ and $\bar c$ of step 1, to the underlying sheaf of sets of $F$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and with $L=K=k$. Then $H_L=\operatorname{Gal}(k/k)=\{1\}$, so $M^{H_L}=M=F_{\bar c}$, and the bijection of that node is restriction to the chosen lift of $\bar c$ over $\operatorname{Spec}L=C$, which is $\bar c$ itself: it is the germ map $\gamma_F:F(C)\to F_{\bar c}$, $t\mapsto$ the class of the triple $(C,\bar c,t)$ in the colimit of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. So $\gamma_F$ is bijective and natural in morphisms of sheaves. For an abelian sheaf the stalk is the colimit of the abelian groups $F(U)$ and $\gamma_F$ is the coprojection at the index $(C,\bar c)$, a homomorphism; hence $\gamma_F$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups, natural in $F\in\Ab(C_{\Et})$. Since $F(C)=\Gamma(C,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] ($C$ is the terminal object of $C_{\Et}$), $\gamma$ is a natural isomorphism of functors $\Gamma(C,-)\cong(-)_{\bar c}:\Ab(C_{\Et})\to\textit{Ab}$.

source.place: Lemma 04JM (lemma-global-sections-point): $\Gamma(S,\mathcal F)=(\mathcal F_{\bar s})^G$, with $G$ trivial

proof.text: *$\Gamma(C,-)$ is exact.* By [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] the stalk functor $F\mapsto F_{\bar c}$ on $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ is exact. Transport along the natural isomorphism $\gamma$ of step 2: $\Gamma(C,-)$ is additive (morphisms of abelian sheaves are added sectionwise), and for a short exact sequence $0\to F'\xrightarrow{a}F\xrightarrow{b}F''\to0$ in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ naturality gives $\gamma_F\circ a_C=a_{\bar c}\circ\gamma_{F'}$ and $\gamma_{F''}\circ b_C=b_{\bar c}\circ\gamma_F$, so the isomorphisms $\gamma_{F'},\gamma_F,\gamma_{F''}$ carry $0\to F'(C)\to F(C)\to F''(C)\to0$ onto the exact sequence of stalks, and it is exact. So $\Gamma(C,-)$ is exact and, by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], commutes with finite limits and finite colimits. (In the language of Lemma 03QU: under the equivalence of $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ with discrete $G$-modules, $G=\{1\}$, the functor $\Gamma$ becomes $M\mapsto M^G=M$, the identity of $\textit{Ab}$.)

source.place: Lemma 03QU (lemma-compare-cohomology-point), proof: 'Combine Lemma 04JQ with Lemma 04JM'; here invariants of the trivial group are the identity functor

proof.text: *Vanishing in positive degrees.* By step 1, $k$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed], so [lem-kun-03qu-sep-closed], applied to $K=k$ and the abelian sheaf $F$, gives $H^q(C_{\Et},F)=0$ for every $q>0$, cohomology being that of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. (This is Lemma 03QU (3), $H^q(C,F)=H^q(G,F_{\bar c})$, for the trivial group $G$; directly, it also follows from step 3 exactly as in step 5 below with $p\ge1$, since $H^p(F[0])=0$ for $p\neq0$.)

*Degree zero.* By [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $H^0(C,F)=H^0(\Gamma(C,I^\bullet))$ for a K-injective resolution $s:F[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], a quasi-isomorphism from $F$ placed in degree $0$; so $H^0(s):F=H^0(F[0])\to H^0(I^\bullet)=Z^0(I^\bullet)/B^0(I^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and it is induced by $s^0:F\to Z^0(I^\bullet)$ ($d^0s^0=s^1\circ0=0$). By step 3 $\Gamma(C,-)$ is exact, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives an isomorphism $c^0:H^0(\Gamma(C,I^\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(C,H^0(I^\bullet))$ compatible with the inclusion of cycles and the projection onto cohomology. Let $\epsilon_F:F(C)\to H^0(C,F)$, $t\mapsto$ the class of $s^0(t)\in Z^0(\Gamma(C,I^\bullet))$. By that compatibility $c^0(\epsilon_F(t))$ is the image of $s^0(t)$ under $\Gamma(C,Z^0(I^\bullet)\to H^0(I^\bullet))$, which is $\Gamma(C,H^0(s))(t)$; so $\epsilon_F=(c^0)^{-1}\circ\Gamma(C,H^0(s))$ is an isomorphism, natural in $F$ because $s$ (up to the identifications of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]) and $c^0$ are. The canonical map of the statement is $\gamma_F\circ\epsilon_F^{-1}:H^0(C,F)\to F_{\bar c}$, a composite of two isomorphisms (step 2 and this step), hence an isomorphism of abelian groups natural in $F$.
